text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 alert — canary cohort 12 latency spike after hotpatch deploy (prefetch optimization). 95p jumped from ~180ms -> ~2.3s, throughput down ~40%, kernel-fallback events increasing. paging on-call.

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-15T10:12Z "hotpatch/prefetch-v2" to canary (10%) by josh — commit abc1234.

alex: ack. moving in. what did the hotpatch change?

sarah: prefetch now does aggressive lookahead for user sessions, should reduce cold-starts but might increase KV pressure. recommend immediate mitigation: either flip flag or rollback canary.

tim: looking at runtime logs from the canary slice, see repeated kernel fallback and prefetch saturating the request queues. excerpt:```
[2026-03-15T10:13:02Z] kernel: fallback_to_cpu=true reason=kernel_unavail
[2026-03-15T10:13:02Z] runtime: prefetch.enq=4821 prefetch.deq=147
[2026-03-15T10:13:05Z] sched: queue_depth=278 cpu_load=0.93
```
josh: if it's queue saturation + fallback, flipping the prefetch flag should be fastest. Can someone flip the kill-switch?

miguel: I can flip the runtime flag now. will flip prefetch.enabled=false for cohort 12 via config-service.

alex: do it and watch latency. also put a hold on new canary promotions.

miguel: running:```bash
curl -X POST https://config.redwood.internal/flags/prefetch -d '{"cohort":12,"value":false}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CFG_TOKEN'
```

miguel: done — config push accepted. deploying flag to canary nodes.

josh: deploy-bot — can you confirm nodes pulled new config?

deploy-bot: config rollout to cohort 12 initiated. agents acked: 5/6, will force push on remaining nodes.

tim: seeing immediate tail latency drop on 3 nodes, others still warming. kernel-fallbacks dropping in logs.

alex: good. can we also pause autoscaler triggers? we saw noisy scaling during the burst.

sarah: paused autoscaler for canary group. traffic shaping to 5% now.

incident-bot: Created INC-2026-0457: "canary-prefetch-hotpatch-latency" — responders: alex, sarah, tim, miguel, josh. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-0457

josh: to be safe, I'm going to roll back the hotpatch from canary -> stable revert pending. anyone object?

amiguel: (typo) — no objections, proceed.

josh: rolling back canary hotpatch:```bash
deploy-bot rollback --deploy-id abc1234 --targets=cohort12 --reason "post-deploy latency spike"
```

deploy-bot: rollback job started. will report when traffic fully shifted.

miguel: metrics: 95p at 10:22 local -> 480ms (partial), 10:24 -> 230ms. throughput back to ~98% of baseline by 10:30.

alex: confirm customer impact — which tenants saw errors/slowdowns?

sarah: pulled usage: 8 enterprise tenants had elevated 5xx/latency alerts, two reported degraded UX in support channel. reaching out to SRE/Sales for proactive comms.

tim: root cause hypothesis: prefetch increased unique KV keys per request pattern causing cache churn and forcing kernel fallback when device memory contended. will reproduce in staging with synthetic fanout.

josh: deploy-bot reports rollback complete, traffic for cohort 12 back to stable model image. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: rollback finished at 2667001800. no urgent failures during traffic shift.

miguel: final metrics snapshot: 95p=210ms, p50=55ms, throughput ~101% baseline. kernel-fallback events returned to baseline.

alex: thanks. next steps: eng-runtime to own postmortem, add guardrails (circuit-breaker on prefetch, throttled rollout, more granular canary slices), update release checklist.

sarah: creating follow-up ticket ACTION-2026-089: "prefetch: add circuit breaker + metrics" and assigning to eng-runtime.

tim: will add a repro harness and synthetic workload to stress KV cache and validate mitigations.

josh: oncall handoff — miguel will keep watch for 1h, then pass to evening oncall.

miguel: oncall ack, will monitor dashboards and customer channels.

incident-bot: Marking incident as "mitigated". Status: P1 -> Mitigated. Pending postmortem.

alex: quick customer impact note for CS: two customers got degraded experience, reach out with timeline and apology, offer assistance. assign to sarah to coordinate.

sarah: will coordinate outreach and include metrics screenshot.

josh: small retrospective note — aggressive prefetch should have been gated behind sampling and mem-pressure checks. adding to postmortem.

tim: tagging perf lead for kernel-affinity tuning in case we need to hard-isolate inference kernels next time.

miguel: thanks all. will follow up in the postmortem with logs and timeline. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Closing thread — follow-up tickets: INC-2026-0457 (mitigated), ACTION-2026-089 (engineering), PM-2026-014 (customer comms).
